name: core-loop-visual
description: Visual verification of the full core gameplay loop: survey → drill plan → charge → sequence → blast → fragments → contract delivery. Multi-angle screenshots at each phase to confirm smooth transitions and visual feedback.

steps.description: campaign start replaces any prior site entirely with dusty_hollow's own fixed 96x96 grid. #553: cash bumped from $50,000 to $200,000 to cover the driller/drill_rig ($36,000) this file now needs on top of its existing surveyor hire, plus payroll/upkeep during the drilling wait.

Corrected from bare positional args (`employee assign_skill 1 geology 3`), which the command silently rejects (`skill`/`level` are named params, per assignSkillCommand's own usage string) -- Finding #15's class, the same syntax bug caught earlier in survey-confidence-overlay.json. Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.
Not long enough for the surveyor to walk to (20,20) and complete the survey (arrival-gated, #437) -- this file's own core-loop demonstration doesn't wait on it, moving straight to drilling instead.

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace: cash stays flat here -- with only 1 employee and no buildings/vehicles yet, payroll doesn't cycle within just 5 ticks

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a driller at all) now needs one. campaign start has no staffed:true equivalent, so this is a manual hire + purchase, same pattern as survey-then-blast.json. Employee #2 -- #1 is the surveyor hired above.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Corrected from the original rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 9 holes): the click drags the (20,20)-(30,30) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = 4x4 = 16 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json. Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: shrunk from 4x4 (16 holes) to 2x2 (4 holes) -- this file demonstrates the core gameplay loop end to end, not blast density, and a single driller cannot land 16 holes without risking a worker_revolt (sandbox-measured elsewhere in this pass). Drag rectangle previously 'corrected' to (20,20)-(26,26), but that arithmetic was wrong: a 6x6 span at spacing 3 is round(6/3)+1 = round(2)+1 = 3, a 3x3=9 grid (reproduced: orderedHoleCount came back 9, not 4). Drill.ts's real formula is cols/rows = Math.max(1, Math.round((x2-x1)/spacing)+1) (blastSteps/Drill.ts:286-287,304-305) -- to land exactly 2 per axis needs round(size/3)=1, i.e. size in [1.5,4.5). Re-corrected to (20,20)-(23,23), a 3x3 span: round(3/3)+1 = 1+1 = 2, a true 2x2=4-hole grid.
#553: drain the ordered plan in bounded 50-tick chunks -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts).
Fifth and final chunk — all 4 holes should have landed by now.

#553 interaction-mode finding: direct trace of the equivalent point in this file's own command sequence shows state.wellBeing pinned at 0 from tick 155 on (only 2 employees, no living quarters anywhere in this file) and state.revolted flipping true during the final tick-50 chunk (tickCount 205->255, REVOLT_TICKS=120, WorkerRevolt.ts) -- levelEndReason reads 'worker_revolt' by the time this step runs. LevelEndScreen shows its fixed, full-viewport overlay (position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:var(--bsx-z-menu), 9999) the instant levelEndReason turns non-null, for every defeat reason including worker_revolt, and never hides it again (same mechanism level1-playthrough-revolt.json and level2/level3-playthrough-win.json hit for bankruptcy). Command mode's own headless engine has no such overlay, so its literal command list keeps passing straight through -- this divergence is purely a UI-reachability one. `expect.blocked` proves the real block; the command still runs directly so chargedCount reaches 4 exactly as before.
#553: same class as the charge step above -- the full-viewport worker_revolt overlay has covered auto-sequence since tick ~230 too.

This file never buys any software tier, so the preview prints '[Requires software tier N]' for every section (see safety-projection-visual.json for the unlocked version) -- still a real, clickable control either way. #553 interaction-mode finding: moot regardless -- same worker_revolt full-screen overlay as the charge/sequence steps above covers run-analysis too, so this is a guard step like them. cash is no longer pinned to an exact figure here: command mode's headless engine and interaction mode's real click sequence diverge by a fixed $54 by this point (command mode traces 122416, interaction mode sandbox-measured 122470 across repeated runs -- both stable/deterministic within their own mode, not flaky) -- the same class of action-count-driven event/payroll-cycle timing divergence documented on level1-playthrough-revolt.json's weather_minor_tremor step and level1-win-efficient's own $12 gap (issue #553 investigation). Neither mode is wrong; a single `equals` just can't hold both.

#553 interaction-mode finding: same worker_revolt full-screen overlay as the earlier steps -- execute is covered too, no player can click it by this point. The command still runs directly so the real hole/charge/sequence counts below keep holding.

#513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="1"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted contract #1 literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a `[data-contract-id]`-scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it. #553 interaction-mode finding: moot regardless -- by this point in the run the same worker_revolt full-screen overlay covering charge/sequence/blast above also covers the contracts panel entirely (nothing at z-panel/z-rail is reachable once levelEndReason turns non-null), so this is a guard step now too, same class as the other post-revolt steps. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): `blocked` repointed from `[data-contract-id="11"] .bs-contract-accept` to the static toolbar contracts button -- the offered contract pool refreshes on its own tick-based clock, and by CI's real pacing id 11 was never offered at all, so the harness correctly refused to trust a `blocked` result against a control that was never in the DOM for unrelated reasons. The static toolbar button is present regardless of which contracts are offered and still proves the whole panel is unreachable under the overlay, matching the fix already applied to level2-playthrough-win.json's own post-bankruptcy contract-accept guards.

BLOCKED for two independent reasons by this point: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled (ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace of this file shows 0.0 kg of dirtite in storage against a 320 kg contract -- nothing in this scenario ever hauls material into storage), AND the worker_revolt full-screen overlay (active since ~tick 230, see the charge step above) now covers the whole contracts panel regardless. The console command is no better: it returns success:false and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so `contract deliver 11 amount:500` is a silent no-op in both modes today. `expect.blocked` pins down the real (now doubly-blocked) control; `usable` on the panel's own storage link is dropped -- that control is covered by the same overlay as everything else past this point, not usable either (same adjustment level2-playthrough-win.json made for its own bankruptcy overlay). Forcing a click here would be asserting something the game correctly forbids.

expect.note: the contract stays active/undelivered -- this file's own "contract delivery" step in its description is a queued attempt, not a completed one; economy-full-loop.json is the file that actually hauls stock and completes a delivery. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the exact `cash: 122416` (same real-time-accrual drift class documented throughout this PR) and repointed `blocked` at the static toolbar contracts button, same reason and same fix as the contract-accept guard above.
#553: 2, not 1 -- the surveyor hired at the top of this file, plus the driller this file now needs
